answer: Picture the economy as a hillside of knolls: each identity claims one, but a sybil operator plants a row of identical ones. The defense is behavioral fingerprinting with a shared weight cap. Every agent leaves a trail — response latencies, vocabulary, tool-call order — and the network clusters identities whose trails match too closely. A cluster shares one weight cap, so a spiral of copied identities earns no more than one honest agent. Faking distinctness per copy costs as much as being real; the velvet touch is that honest agents feel nothing, only the swarm feels the cap.
